newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower as soybeans and oats falter.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower as soybeans and oats falter.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on a sharp break in the soybean market plus a tumble in oats which was triggered by a surge in the volume of oat delivery notices, traders said.
Fund selling, estimated at least 20 million bushels, led the way down, the traders said.
Lee B. Stern and Co sold 12 million bushels of March and E.D. and F. Man sold at least three million bushels of March, traders said.
But many cited the fall in soybeans and oats as a key catalyst for the declines in the corn pit.
The soybean market was hit by nearly ideal crop weather in South America plus followthrough fund selling after a weak close Friday.

Traders said the oat delivery notices posted Monday against the December at 4.6 million bushels hit the oat market. Oats closed four to 5-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with December down 5-1/4 at $1.44-3/4.
Some traders said a hike in farmer selling of corn also lent pressure to the market.
Corn closed four to 5-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with December down 4-1/4 at $2.66-1/2.
